definition: A being that is more a being than every distinct being. Under a strict comparative order this implies uniqueness and comparability of every other being with it; the arbitrary MoreIn parameter of the generic readings does not itself supply that order law.
note: Recorded as the strict-supremacy sense, so that the merely-maximal maxime ens is not silently strengthened to it. Existing degree-fork and control statements use or contrast this stronger reading; uniqueness of a merely maximal being still requires its separate argument (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-AT-MOST-ONE-MAXIME-ENS). Current typed uses include STMT-QUARTA-VIA-STRICT-CAUSAL-TOP, STMT-QUARTA-VIA-DEGREE-FORK, STMT-QUARTA-VIA-UNBOUNDED-DEGREES, STMT-QUARTA-VIA-DEGREE-BRANCH-WITNESSES and STMT-INFINITE-GREATEST-WHOLE-CONTROL. In TruthCore.Latin.Aquinas.SummaTheologiae.QuartaViaStrictCausalTop the strict comparative clause is ∀ x, x ≠ m → MoreIn esse m x; that surrounding predicate adds separate maximality and causal conditions which are not part of this term alone. Before sense fork batch 3 there was no standalone declaration for just this raw strict clause. TruthCore.Causality.MaximumDefinitionFork.StrictGreatest instead uses represented degrees and must not be substituted without the explicit comparative calibration. The intended relation/order interpretation remains OPEN. In particular, the raw strict clause alone need not force uniqueness if MoreIn can hold in both directions; uniqueness requires the stated strict-order/calibration background rather than the word greatest. This qualification concerns the raw supremacy clause alone: QuartaViaStrictCausalTop separately conjoins maximality and its uniqueness clause, so no new asymmetry premise is imposed on that full predicate. Sense fork batch 3 (MAXIME_3): StrictlyGreatestIn InAct MoreIn r m := InAct m r ∧ ∀ x, x ≠ m → MoreIn r m x is now the standalone declaration of exactly this strict clause plus possession of r; it adds no maximality, uniqueness or causal condition.
